references.sentence: Fig. 1 shows an area-efficient overall chip architecture of the 288-Mb DRAM consisting of the stacked 32 banks (16 banks for each top and bottom) of 9-Mb cell arrays per bank.
The high-speed interface circuit block in the middle of the Fig. 1 consists of high-speed I/O circuitry, control logic including DRAM interface, and a delay-locked loop (DLL).

For read or write operation, 144 I/O lines from these two-diagonal mats are connected to global pipeline and I/O-sense amplifier (S/A) and write-driver block which consists of 144 I/O-S/As and 144 write drivers with prefetch registers, resulting in the reduction of die Fig. 1.

figures.section_title: III. DRAM CORE TIMING MARGIN ENHANCEMENT

references.sentence: Further reduction of chip size penalty can be achieved using mixture of DRAM peripheral circuits with the high-speed interface circuits as shown in Fig. 4.

In the conventional architecture in Fig. 4(a), not only repeatable logic circuits but also random circuits for address and command input buffers and control clock generator are placed for each of memory arrays, which requires additional circuit layers.

But, in this work, random circuits for four memory arrays are gathered in the RAS and CAS CONTROL block to increase the overall area efficiency by reducing circuit layers, as in Fig. 4(b), which achieves the die size reduction of 1.5%.
